countries_thin_or_null: Myanmar — still thin on recent primary sources for labour or CPI methodology upgrades

dependencies.basis: National accounts residual employment approach for the unorganized sector derives employment as the residual of Labor Force Survey (LFS) employment and establishment surveys (CPBI/ASPBI).
dependencies.evidence_quote: To come up with the GVA of the unorganized industry, indirect estimation is employed using the residual employment approach. Using this approach, employment in the unorganized industry is derived as the residual of the employment of the Labor Force Survey (LFS) and the Census of Philippine Business and Industry (CPBI) for the benchmark year or the Annual Survey of Philippine Business and Industry (ASPBI) for the non-benchmark years.

dependencies.basis: Personal remittances / cash remittances from overseas Filipinos form a major component of the secondary income account (personal transfers) in the BPM6-based BOP.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The BPM6 identifies the standard components and provides supplementary items to allow compilation of remittance aggregates. The standard components of remittances refer to the compensation of employees (lodged under the Primary Income account) and personal transfers (lodged under the Secondary Income account).

dependencies.basis: Philippine Labor Force Survey follows international labour statistics standards consistent with ICLS resolutions for employment and unemployment concepts.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The sources of data and the methodology are being reviewed by the Inter-Agency Committee on Labor and Productivity Statistics (IACLPS).

dependencies.basis: Vietnam CPI compilation follows international statistical practice and has plans for improving structure by the latest COICOP; weights derived from household living standards surveys.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Improving consumer price index structure by the latest COICOP ... The weights used in calculating CPI is derived from the Vietnam Household Living Standard Survey (VHLSS) and CPI weights survey.

dependencies.basis: Thailand CPI classification is consistent with the UN COICOP classification (developed corresponding to the household expenditure survey).
dependencies.evidence_quote: The classification system was developed by the Bureau of Trade and Economic Indices (BTEI) corresponding to the household expenditure survey conducted by National Statistics Office (NSO) which is consistent with the UN COICOP classification.

dependencies.basis: Thailand national accounts industry classifications align with international standards including ISIC adaptations used in the statistical system.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Both of the annual national accounts and the QGDP are in line with the 2008 SNA, with chained volume measures to express the constant terms.
